status_legend.in_progress: The feature is the current active task (at most one at a time).
status_legend.blocked: Work cannot continue until the blocker in `notes` is resolved.
status_legend.passing: Required verification ran and the evidence is recorded.

features.title: Self-hosting bootstrap
features.user_visible_behavior: The harness repository is a harness project: ./init.sh, pnpm harness:doctor and pnpm check pass, and pnpm harness:loop can build features from harness-retro issues.
features.notes: Retro features are added by the loop's intake (docs/self-improvement.md).

features.title: Loop sessions cannot launch the evaluator agent
features.user_visible_behavior: In a driver-run session (HARNESS_LOOP=1) the guard denies an Agent/Task call for the harness:evaluator subagent with a reason that says the driver runs the evaluator; interactive sessions can still launch it. The generator and CI-fixer prompts and the clock-out skill say the same.
features.notes: Found 2026-10-24 in the overnight loops of idea-generator, personal-finances and metsavahti: about 15 generator sessions launched harness:evaluator before clock-out and idled on ScheduleWakeup for it, although clock-out step 7 says to skip it under HARNESS_LOOP=1. The driver evaluates anyway, so the review ran twice.

features.title: Session stats count every turn of a resumed session
features.user_visible_behavior: When a stream-json session emits several result messages (it was resumed by a wakeup or a background-task notification), runs.jsonl, the PR body and harness report show the sum of their num_turns, not only the last segment.
features.notes: personal-finances F-015 attempt 1 emitted results with 87, 18 and 2 turns; runs.jsonl recorded 2. Several $3–10 sessions show 1–4 turns. total_cost_usd is already cumulative.

features.title: Queue-empty notice lists only unmerged feature branches
features.user_visible_behavior: The queue-empty notice no longer names features that are already passing on the default branch as in flight; it names their leftover branches separately so a human can delete them.
evidence: 2026-10-24 pnpm check → pass (working tree on a2a17d1)
features.notes: idea-generator feat/F-006 and personal-finances feat/F-002 survived their merges (the first merge before delete_branch_on_merge was on), so every queue-empty notice said they were in flight.

features.title: Merges that change the package are released automatically
features.user_visible_behavior: After CI passes on main, a release workflow bumps the version (patch by default; minor for a breaking change while 0.x), adds a CHANGELOG entry from the commit subjects, commits chore: release vX.Y.Z, tags it, pushes and creates the GitHub release. Merges that change no shipped path (docs, tests, state files) release nothing.
evidence: 2026-10-24 pnpm check → pass (working tree on eb4150a)
features.notes: Requested 2026-10-24: the self-improvement loop merges to main, but the changes reach projects only after a human cuts a release. main is protected, so the workflow pushes with a RELEASE_TOKEN secret that may bypass the protection.

features.title: Project loops update to the newest harness release before each feature
features.user_visible_behavior: With update.auto, before picking a feature the loop driver checks for a newer harness release; it opens a harness/update-vX.Y.Z PR that changes only the package pin and the plugin marketplace ref (checked with doctor and the L1 baseline), auto-merges it when the merge policy is auto, pulls, reinstalls and restarts itself on the new version. harness update [--check] does the same by hand. Off by default.
evidence: 2026-10-24 pnpm check → pass (working tree on da91493)
features.notes: Requested 2026-10-24: updating every project by hand in the middle of a loop is the bottleneck once releases are automatic (F-004). Breaking releases need update.allowBreaking.

features.title: Selftest, schema-based breaking detection and the harness version on run records
features.user_visible_behavior: harness selftest checks a project with the installed harness: config and feature list load, prompts render, the evaluator agent parses, the guard still blocks its core cases and still allows the project allowedTools and verification commands, the lifecycle hooks exit cleanly, doctor is ok; it runs in the harness repository check. The release script treats a removed, newly required, re-defaulted or narrowed config key as a breaking change. Every runs.jsonl record names its harness version and harness report shows it.
evidence: 2026-10-24 pnpm check → pass (working tree on bbc9a95)
features.notes: Requested 2026-10-24: automatic updates must not let a harness regression spread. Loop PR titles never carry !, so breaking changes must be found from the schema.

features.title: Staged rollout and quarantine of harness releases
features.user_visible_behavior: With update.auto the loop takes the newest release that is at least update.minAgeHours old (default 6, 0 for a canary), not a draft or prerelease and not quarantined. A version is quarantined by an open or completed harness-quarantine issue in the harness repository; closing it as not planned lifts it. A project on a quarantined version moves to the newest eligible release or back to an older one. The update PR runs the old and the new selftest; a check that regresses quarantines the release with the evidence instead of opening the PR.
features.notes: Requested 2026-10-24: catch a bad release in one project and keep it from reaching the others.

features.title: Probation, rollback and re-test after a harness update
features.user_visible_behavior: The first feature after an update runs on probation. If it fails, is blocked or the driver errors, its branch is kept as harness/probation-vX-F-NNN and removed from the queue, the project rolls back to the previous release through a pin-only PR and re-runs the feature there. Passing on the old version quarantines the release with both outcomes; failing again clears it. The previous driver supervises the restarted one and rolls back and quarantines when it exits with an error before a probation result.
evidence: 2026-10-24 pnpm check → pass (working tree on a2ecf8e)
features.notes: Requested 2026-10-24: a harness regression must not burn feature attempts and must be traced to the release that caused it.

features.title: Canary rollout: the first loop tests a release, the others take only verified ones
features.user_visible_behavior: Each release gets a rollout issue in the harness repository. The first project loop with update.auto and update.canary that starts a feature claims the release there (earliest active claim comment wins), updates and runs its probation, renewing the claim while it tests. A pass marks the release verified; other projects take only verified releases. A claim lapses after update.canaryHours (default 4) without renewal, so another loop may take over. A failed update or an inconclusive re-test releases the claim; a quarantine closes the rollout issue.
features.notes: Requested 2026-10-24: replace the fixed waiting time (update.minAgeHours, unreleased) with a first-come canary, so no project takes a release nobody tested. The 4 h the user called the quarantine time is the claim window.

features.title: Quarantine issues carry a log excerpt and absolute trace paths
features.user_visible_behavior: A quarantine issue filed after a failed probation, a re-test or a driver crash includes an excerpt of the failing run readable log (telling lines and the end of the run, within the 3000 characters the intake keeps) and the absolute paths of that log and its traces, so the harness loop session that builds the fix can read the failure.
features.notes: Requested 2026-10-24: the evidence named traces relative to the project, so a fixing session in the harness repository could not open them.

features.title: Retro intake can be gated on a triage label
features.user_visible_behavior: With retro.intakeLabel set, the loop intake takes only open retro issues that also carry that label; unset keeps todays behaviour. The package exports the issue, quarantine and rollout readers a triage service needs (parseIssueFeature, fingerprintOf, issueContext, quarantinedVersions, rolloutStates and the label names).
features.notes: Requested 2026-10-24 for harness-updater: a Docker service that validates each harness issue against the consumer repositories before the harness loop builds it.

features.title: Driver-started sessions get no GitHub token
features.user_visible_behavior: Every Claude session the loop or the retro starts (generator, evaluator, safety review, CI fixer, retro analysis) runs without GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN or the enterprise variants and with an empty gh config directory, so gh is logged out inside the session while the driver keeps its own GitHub access.
features.notes: Requested 2026-10-24: harness-updater runs the loop with the owner token in its environment; a session that read injected text (issue, PR, trace) could have used gh as the owner. Sessions never need GitHub: the driver pushes, opens PRs and reads CI.

features.title: Restart onto the version that was actually installed
features.user_visible_behavior: After an update or rollback the driver restarts on the harness now installed in the project, resolved from the file system rather than the process module cache. It refuses to restart when the installed version is not the one the pins moved to, and a restarted driver that is not the version on probation records restart-mismatch and stops; the supervisor treats that as settled and neither rolls back nor quarantines.
features.notes: Found 2026-10-24 in metsavahti: after updating to v0.3.2 and later v0.3.3 the driver logged restarted on harness v0.3.1. require.resolve returned the cached real path of the old package, so the child ran v0.3.1 code against v0.3.2 pins, failed the doctor with exit 1, and the supervisor rolled back and quarantined v0.3.2 (issue #11), a false alarm. Every release up to v0.3.4 has this restart bug in the parent, so projects need one hand update to the fix.

features.title: Keep a restarted driver output for the evidence
features.user_visible_behavior: When the driver restarts itself on a new harness release, the new driver output is shown in the terminal and also written to .harness/traces/driver-vX.Y.Z-<time>.log. If that driver exits non-zero before its first feature settles, the rollback PR names its error line, and the quarantine issue carries the error line in its cause, an excerpt of the output and the log path.
features.notes: Proposed by harness-updater triage of harness #11 (2026-10-24): that quarantine said only that the driver exited with code 1, because the restarted driver wrote to the terminal only; the cause (F-013) was found in a terminal transcript.
